prompt: A table shows $x: 1, 2, 3$ and $y: 9, 13, 17$. The $y$-values jump by the same amount each step. What is the slope $m$?
hint: When $x$ goes up by $1$ each time, the slope is the amount $y$ changes at each step.

hints.text: When $x$ goes up by $1$ each time, the slope is the amount $y$ changes at each step.
Subtract neighbouring $y$-values: find $13 - 9$ and $17 - 13$ and check that they agree.
Both differences are $4$, so the slope of the line is $m = 4$.

explanation: The $x$-values go up by $1$ each time, while the $y$-values go $9$, $13$, $17$.
Find each jump by subtracting: $13 - 9 = 4$ and $17 - 13 = 4$.
The $y$-value rises by a constant $4$ for every $1$ step in $x$, so the slope is $m = 4$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Slope formula
steps: Take two rows as points: $(1, 9)$ and $(3, 17)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rate story
steps: Read the table as pay: hour $1 \to \$9$, hour $2 \to \$13$, hour $3 \to \$17$.
You earn $\$4$ more every hour — that per-hour rate is the slope, $4$.
